transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical support. My name is Connor. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Connor. My name is Benjamin Vance. I have an urgent and critical problem with my broadband connection at home that is severely affecting my remote software engineering work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning Benjamin. Before we examine your broadband connection and line statistics, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 82 Parkside Avenue, Bristol, BS6 5TN, and my security PIN is 4481.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Benjamin, that successfully verifies your account. What seems to be happening with your broadband service today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My upload speed has completely cratered to half a megabit! I manage a software development team remotely, and all morning my Zoom calls keep freezing and disconnecting in front of executive directors! It's utterly humiliating and causing massive disruption!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how disruptive and stressful it is when your video conferences freeze during critical executive meetings, Benjamin. Let me pull up your line diagnostics and optical sync parameters.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Connor. We have the S-Net Hub 5 full-fibre router installed in the main hallway right next to the optical termination wall box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is your desktop work computer physically connected to the Hub 5 router right now across your home office?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am plugged directly into gigabit Ethernet port 1 with a brand new Cat 6 shielded cable. No Wi-Fi involved whatsoever on this primary workstation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me test the physical optical link power levels and upstream sync rate from our network management diagnostic platform.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Go ahead, I am looking at the live Ookla speed test telemetry graph right now on my desktop monitor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I run the full spectrum time-domain reflectometry and upstream packet loss test on your fibre drop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, I will wait.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Benjamin. The optical power reading on the downstream is minus eighteen dBm, which is completely within normal operating thresholds for full fibre.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, downloading data is completely fine, I reliably get 300 megabits down. It is strictly the upload direction that is choked down to 0.5 megabits per second.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I run the upstream attenuation test, that is the Hub 5 router, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, as I mentioned, it is the Hub 5 wireless router unit in the hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our upstream sync profile is showing severe burst noise and signal attenuation on the return path frequency band across the local distribution loop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does that mean in practical terms for my daily upload traffic and video conferencing bandwidth?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It means high packet retransmissions on your upstream queue, which throttles your upload throughput down to half a megabit while downstream browsing remains completely unaffected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you reset the line profile, clear the session buffers, or re-profile the port from your network operations terminal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an issue on the local street node multiplexer in your area. S-Net frontline support cannot dispatch or fix street node infrastructure; that is handled by Openreach civil engineering contractors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, I just ran another test while we are speaking and the upload dropped to 0.3 Mbps! I have our quarterly board presentation in forty-five minutes! If my connection drops during the CEO's review I could genuinely lose my job! You have to do something now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how alarming and stressful that is with your board presentation forty-five minutes away, Benjamin. I know how critical that meeting is for your career.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then what can you do to fix this street node immediately before my executive presentation starts in thirty minutes?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well if you actually paid attention to our fair usage and residential service terms, you would know home residential broadband isn't an enterprise leased line with dedicated engineer callouts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is no need to be rude, sarcastic, and condescending! I am paying premium rates for your top-tier full fibre package and expect professional support!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All I can do is raise a standard fault ticket with the network operations queue. The standard response window is two to three business days for external roadside cabinet investigations.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Two to three business days? That does not help me for today's critical executive meeting in forty minutes at all!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you testing your computer over Wi-Fi or do you have an Ethernet cable plugged directly into the router right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I already told you at the very beginning of the call that I am plugged directly into port 1 with a Cat 6 shielded Ethernet cable, not running on Wi-Fi!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fine. I will formally document and log the fault ticket for the regional street cabinet engineering team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the official incident reference number for this roadside engineering fault ticket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Give me a moment while our internal network engineering ticketing application registers the fault report and assigns a tracking priority code.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Benjamin. Your network fault reference number has been created as FLT-782190-UP in our operations engineering portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: FLT-782190-UP, noted down. And what should I do right now for my impending executive board presentation?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will need to use your 4G or 5G mobile hotspot from your mobile handset provider as a backup data connection for your video conference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I suppose that's my only option. So the broadband itself is not fixed on this call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, it cannot be fixed until the cabinet engineers investigate the physical line card and the upstream noise floor at the exchange cabinet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you email me an official summary transcript of this support call so I have documentation to show my senior management team?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Call audio transcripts cannot be emailed, but all ticket diagnostic logs are saved to your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. I will prepare my mobile hotspot then.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else on your account I can assist with today, Benjamin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Am I entitled to compensation under the automatic compensation scheme for this upload drop?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Ofcom automatic compensation scheme applies only to total loss of broadband service or missed engineer appointments, not degraded upload speeds on an active line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That seems very one-sided given how much I pay each month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Those are the standard regulatory guidelines established by the telecom ombudsman across all UK internet service providers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, my router just restarted its optical session! Did you trigger something?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I sent an automated port bounce and profile reset to the street multiplexer line card before logging the fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test it... it just hit 65 Mbps upload! The video conference preview is completely smooth and crystal clear now! That actually fixed it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The port reset cleared the buffer noise. That confirms your upload throughput is fully restored to standard speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is such a relief for my meeting, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net broadband technical support, Benjamin.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Connor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.
